name: Tiroler Kaiserjägermuseum
kurzbeschreibung: The Tyrolean Kaiserjäger Museum on Bergisel in Innsbruck: founded in 1880, one of the oldest military museums worldwide dedicated to the history of the four Imperial and Royal Kaiserjäger regiments.
beschreibung:
Overview

The historic Tyrolean Kaiserjäger Museum is perched on the traditional Bergisel plateau at 746 meters above sea level in the south of the provincial capital Innsbruck. Nestled in a well-maintained park directly adjacent to the modern museum complex Das Tirol Panorama and the Bergisel ski jump, the museum serves as the historical memory of the four famous Imperial and Royal Tyrolean Kaiserjäger regiments. Founded on October 4, 1880, it is one of the oldest independent regimental and military museums in the world, shedding light on a central chapter of Tyrolean and Old Austrian contemporary history.

Route & Requirements

The Kaiserjäger Museum is easily accessible and requires no special physical demands. It is located on Bergisel, which is well-connected by both public transport and car. The exhibition rooms are spread across several floors, but the entire museum is seamlessly and barrier-free accessible via a modern connecting wing of the Tirol Panorama, with passenger elevators. This allows for a comfortable visit for wheelchair users and families with strollers. A visit to the museum is an indoor activity, making it ideal for all weather conditions. For a comprehensive insight into the history of the Kaiserjäger, one should plan about 1 to 2 hours.

Visit & Arrival

The Tyrolean Kaiserjäger Museum is part of the Tyrolean State Museums and is open year-round from Wednesday to Monday from 09:00 to 17:00 (closed Tuesdays). Admission prices (as of season 2025/2026): Combi-ticket for Das Tirol Panorama with Kaiserjäger Museum: Adults €12.00, Seniors and students €9.00, children and youths under 19 enjoy free admission! With the Innsbruck Card, admission is free. Arrival by public transport: From Innsbruck main station, take tram line 1 or 6 to the Bergisel stop, or bus line TS (The Sightseer Innsbruck) directly to the museum forecourt. By car: Autobahn A12/A13 (exit Innsbruck Süd or Mitte), paid parking is available at the Bergisel car park.

Tips

The museum is seamlessly and barrier-free accessible for wheelchair users and strollers via the modern connecting wing of the Tirol Panorama, with passenger elevators. After visiting the museum, a stroll along the Bergisel Panorama Trail is worthwhile, offering breathtaking views of the Europa Bridge and the Stubai Valley. The Restaurant 1809 on the museum forecourt serves first-class Tyrolean regional cuisine. Ideally, plan your visit to the Kaiserjäger Museum in combination with the Tirol Panorama and the Giant Panoramic Painting, as both attractions are directly connected and a combi-ticket is offered. This allows for a deep insight into Tyrolean history and culture in one location.
preis: Combi-ticket with Tirol Panorama: Adults €12.00, Children under 19 free
